profile.summary: ModernGENA is a DNA language model that adapts the ModernBERT encoder to genomic sequences. It reads DNA split into byte-pair-encoding (BPE) tokens and was pretrained by masked language modelling on 443 vertebrate genome assemblies. It outputs token embeddings that are fine-tuned for downstream tasks such as sequence classification or per-token regression; the authors present it as an efficient baseline for future DNA model work.
profile.summary_source_locator: Europe PMC abstract; model card: Tokenization, Pretraining corpus; GENA_LM examples README

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ModernGENA is a BERT-style encoder built on ModernBERT. The model card lists RoPE positional embeddings, hybrid local and global attention, pre-norm transformer blocks, GeGLU feed-forward layers and end-to-end unpadding, with FlashAttention for faster inference on compatible hardware. In the published configurations, local attention covers 128 tokens and every third layer uses global attention. Input DNA is tokenised with the 32k BPE vocabulary from GENA-LM over the symbols A, T, G, C and N. Pretraining used masked language modelling on intervals sampled from -16 kbp to +8 kbp around each transcription start site, on both strands, to reduce the weight of simple repeats.

A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision; this page read base at revision 7036ebb6 and large at revision 01de8202. The paper says the full implementation and configuration are released; the fine-tuning examples the card links to live in the GENA_LM repository.

profile.summary: GPN (Genomic Pretrained Network, also called GPN-SS) is a DNA language model that learns from unaligned genome sequences alone. Given a 512-bp DNA window with some positions masked, it predicts the nucleotide at each masked position. Its main use is to score genetic variants without labels: the score is the log-likelihood ratio of the alternate against the reference allele. The published model was trained on Arabidopsis thaliana and seven other Brassicales genomes.
profile.summary_source_locator: docs/models/gpn.md introduction; paper Fig. 1 caption; model card title

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GPN is a convolutional neural network, not a transformer. The masked DNA sequence is one-hot encoded with single nucleotides as tokens, then passed through 25 convolutional blocks. Each block has a dilated convolution and a feed-forward layer, with residual connections and layer normalisation; the embedding dimension stays at 512. Training is masked language modelling: 15% of positions are masked and predicted with a cross-entropy loss. To score a variant, only the variant position is masked, and the score is the log-likelihood ratio of the alternate against the reference allele. The authors down-weighted repetitive elements in the loss; the card records a repeat weight of 0.1.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Materials and Methods, Fig. 1 caption; model card: Some hparams

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The songlab-cal/gpn repository now covers four model families: GPN, GPN-MSA, PhyloGPN and GPN-Star. This page is about single-sequence GPN. Its published checkpoint is songlab/gpn-brassicales, which uses a seven-token DNA tokenizer. The same family also has an animal promoter model (songlab/gpn-animal-promoter) and a sorghum gene-expression model fine-tuned from gpn-brassicales. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision; this page read gpn-brassicales at revision eb9c35d0. The paper analyses are kept in an archive branch, and the maintained training recipe is in recipes/gpn_training. Note that the existing benchmark source (Tang et al. 2025) did not use gpn-brassicales: it evaluated a custom GPN pre-trained on the human reference genome.

profile.summary: HyenaDNA is a family of DNA language models that read very long stretches of genome one base at a time, up to 1 million bases in the largest model. It was pretrained on the human reference genome by predicting the next base, and it outputs per-base embeddings that can be fine-tuned for tasks such as finding regulatory elements or classifying species.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: Intro; model card: Model & Training Overview; arXiv abstract

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: HyenaDNA replaces attention with a stack of Hyena operators, which use input projections, implicit long convolutions and gating and scale sub-quadratically with sequence length. Each layer has a global receptive field. A single-character tokenizer with a vocabulary of the 4 nucleotides plus special tokens keeps single-base resolution. The model is causal: it is pretrained by next-nucleotide prediction on the human reference genome (HG38), and the inference script pads on the left for that reason.

Each exists as a weights-only repository for the original GitHub code and as a transformers-compatible copy with an -hf suffix; the model card says the two give identical outputs. A result should name the checkpoint, which interface was used, and the revision; this page read LongSafari/hyenadna-large-1m-seqlen-hf at revision 0a629abf. A Docker image with the exact Nucleotide Transformer benchmark settings from the paper is also provided.

profile.summary: RNAGenesis is an RNA foundation model that handles sequence representation, structure prediction and sequence design in one framework. A BERT-style encoder, pretrained with masked RNA modelling on non-coding RNAs, turns an RNA sequence into embeddings; a query-based compression step maps those into a short latent code, and a diffusion model generates new latent codes that a decoder turns back into sequences. It is used both to score or classify RNAs after fine-tuning and to design new ones, such as aptamers and CRISPR sgRNA scaffolds.
profile.summary_source_locator: Preprint abstract; README: Overview, Encoder Checkpoint for Embeddings

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The repository's pretraining configuration for the stage-one encoder uses single-nucleotide embeddings of width 1,280, six parallel convolutional layers with kernels 3 to 13 whose outputs are summed with those embeddings, and 32 bidirectional Transformer blocks with 20 attention heads, RoPE and SwiGLU feed-forward layers. Training is masked RNA modelling: 30% of positions are selected and the loss is cross-entropy on those positions only. The repository notes that masking happens before the convolutional embeddings, so the masked bases cannot leak through the convolutions. No source read says which configuration the released Zenodo and Hugging Face weights use. The repository tree also holds two files whose names contain 6layers_16heads_128embedsize. For generation, the encoder output is compressed into a latent code, a diffusion model samples new latent codes, and a decoder produces sequences. Sampling can be steered at inference time by a classifier gradient or by beam search.

sections.title: What it is used for
sections.body: Two routes are documented. For understanding tasks, the pretrained encoder is fine-tuned: the repository's example adds LoRA adapters, averages the valid nucleotide embeddings and trains an MLP head for 13 ncRNA classes. For design, generation.py samples sequences from a diffusion checkpoint, with aptamer and sgRNA checkpoints given as examples, optionally with classifier guidance or beam search. A separate module fine-tunes the encoder for 3D structure prediction.

profile.summary: ViroHyena is a small family of nucleotide language models built on the Hyena architecture by the authors of the ViroBench viral genomics benchmark. They were pretrained on ViroBlend, a 216 Mbp corpus that mixes human reference, multi-species and viral sequences. The models take nucleotide sequences and serve as baselines in ViroBench for viral taxonomy and host classification from embeddings and for likelihood-based genome modelling.

In ViroBench, classification is done with the backbone frozen: a sequence embedding is extracted and a small MLP head is trained on it. profile.summary: BioFM is a genomic foundation model from M42 Health that reads DNA together with biological context. Its BioToken tokeniser encodes genetic variants and annotated regions (such as genes and regulatory elements) directly in the input, instead of treating DNA as bases only. The model produces embeddings for variants or sequences, which are used with simple classifiers to predict effects on expression, splicing and pathogenicity; it can also generate DNA sequence.
profile.summary_source_locator: Europe PMC abstract; model card: Model Details; README: Quick Start

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: BioFM is a decoder-only (causal) transformer on the Mistral architecture, with 23 layers and hidden size 640. Its input is DNA annotated with BioTokens: tokens that carry variant information and genomic annotations alongside the bases. For a variant, the package builds an upstream and a downstream sequence, each ending at the variant and half the evaluation context long; the downstream one is reverse complemented. Reference and mutated embeddings are each averaged over the two directions and then concatenated, giving a vector twice the embedding size. For plain sequences the embedding is taken from the last token. Downstream predictions use linear probing on these embeddings.

profile.summary: TREDNet predicts whether a 2,000 base pair stretch of human DNA acts as an enhancer, and how much a single-nucleotide variant changes that prediction. It works in two stages: a first convolutional network turns the one-hot encoded sequence into 1,924 predicted epigenomic signals (DNase I hypersensitivity, histone modifications and transcription factor binding), and a second, smaller network turns that vector into an enhancer probability for one tissue or cell line. Released phase two models cover pancreatic islets, HepG2 and K562.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Phase one is a multitask convolutional classifier in the style of DeepSEA, Beluga and DanQ. It takes a one-hot encoded 2,000 base window and outputs 1,924 values, one per epigenomic feature. Phase two is a smaller convolutional network trained on enhancer regions, but each region is first passed through phase one and so is represented by the 1,924-value vector rather than by its sequence. Phase two can be a single-output classifier for one tissue or a multitask classifier over several. Chromosomes 8 and 9 were held out of training and used for testing.

sections.title: Scoring variants and regions
sections.body: The repository's score_variant.py reads a VCF, needs an hg19 FASTA, and writes a tab-separated file. With -score-iep it builds the 2,000 base reference and alternate sequences centred on the SNP, predicts both, and scores the variant as the larger probability times the absolute difference between the two. With -score-delta it takes the 2,000 base window around the variant, substitutes every other base at each position from 990 to 1010, averages the drop from the reference prediction at each position and divides by the median absolute value, writing the resulting list of values. Separately, the paper reports saturated mutagenesis across whole enhancers, which it calls enhancer damage (ED) scores, and defines peaks and dips in them as enhancer damaging regions (EDRs) and enhancer strengthening regions (ESRs). A second module, peak_detection/annotate.py, performs what the README calls PAS/DAS detection from a file of precomputed deltas.

profile.summary: DeepGene is a DNA foundation model that learns from a pan-genome graph rather than a single reference sequence, so that genetic variation across individuals is part of what it sees in pretraining. It is a transformer encoder with rotary position embeddings, built to handle sequences of different lengths. The pretrained model is fine-tuned for sequence classification tasks such as promoter prediction and the Genome Understanding Evaluation (GUE) tasks.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The model is a RoFormer, a transformer encoder with rotary position embeddings, pretrained as a masked language model. The code's default configuration has 12 layers, hidden size 768, 12 attention heads, a vocabulary of 4096 tokens and 5120 positions; pretraining builds the model from this default configuration. The pretraining data comes from a Minigraph pan-genome graph: the processing script reads the graph's sequence segments and edges and tokenises them with the repository's tokenizer.json, and pretraining uses subgraphs (default size 128). For downstream tasks the pretrained weights are loaded into a sequence classification model and fine-tuned, with MCC or F1 as the metric.

profile.summary: Evo is a 7-billion-parameter DNA language model trained on prokaryotic whole genomes. It reads DNA one base at a time, with a context of 8,192 or 131,072 bases depending on the checkpoint, and predicts the next base. The developers use it to score how likely a sequence is and to generate new DNA, from single genes and CRISPR-Cas systems up to genome-scale sequences.
profile.summary_source_locator: README.md: introduction and checkpoint table; Usage

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Evo uses the StripedHyena architecture, a hybrid of multi-head attention and gated convolutions arranged in Hyena blocks. Hyena layers do most of the sequence processing and attention layers add targeted pattern recall, which gives near-linear scaling of compute and memory with context length. Tokens are single nucleotides (byte-level). The model is autoregressive: it outputs logits over the vocabulary at each position, which are used to sample new sequence or to score the log-likelihood of an existing one. Generation can run in a recurrent mode; the model card reports more than 500k bases generated on a single 80GB GPU.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: evo-1-8k-base was pretrained at 8,192 context. evo-1-131k-base continues from it at 131,072 context. Evo 1.5 (evo-1.5-8k-base) extends the pretraining of evo-1-8k-base with 50% more data, to 450 billion tokens, and was introduced in a 2025 Nature paper. Two fine-tuned models generate CRISPR-Cas systems and IS200/IS605 transposons. The model card adds 15 intermediate pretraining checkpoints as branches. The Hugging Face weights had a projection-permutation bug that affects generation; the fix is loaded with revision="1.1_fix". The evo-model package had an inference bug in versions installed between Nov 15 and Dec 16, 2024, fixed from release 0.3. profile.summary: eccDNAMamba is a pretrained model for extrachromosomal circular DNA (eccDNA), circular DNA molecules that carry amplified oncogenes in cancer. It reads full-length eccDNA sequences of 10 to 200 kbp, and copies the start of each sequence onto its end so the model sees across the point where the circle was opened. Fine-tuned versions are used for cancer-associated eccDNA prediction, copy-number level estimation, and telling real from pseudo-eccDNA.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: eccDNAMamba is a bidirectional state-space model: forward and reverse Mamba-2 encoders read the sequence in both directions, with cost linear in sequence length. DNA is tokenised by motif-level byte pair encoding (BPE) with a vocabulary of 4096. To respect the circular shape, a head-tail augmentation appends the first 64 tokens after the end of the sequence. The pretrained backbone is a masked language model (BiMambaForMaskedLM) with 24 layers and d_model 768. For classification, the published fine-tuning code mean-pools the hidden states and adds a two-layer classifier head.

profile.summary: GenomeOcean is a family of generative DNA language models trained on co-assembled environmental metagenomes, mainly microbial DNA. It reads DNA split into multi-base tokens and predicts the next token. The developers provide scripts to produce sequence embeddings for analysis and to generate new DNA from a prompt. The largest model has 4 billion parameters and reads up to about 50,000 bases.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GenomeOcean is a decoder-only transformer trained by causal language modelling: it predicts the next token from the tokens before it. DNA is split by a BPE tokenizer with 4096 tokens, so 1024 tokens cover about 5,100 bp. The 4B checkpoint uses the Mistral architecture in transformers, with 24 layers, hidden size 3072, 12 attention heads and 4 key/value heads. The package uses vLLM for fast generation and also produces sequence embeddings. The developers report that the model captures universal phylogenetic syntax and protein-coding fidelity, and that its embeddings have low intrinsic dimensionality.

sections.body: Three base models are published: GenomeOcean-100M and GenomeOcean-500M with a 1024-token context, and GenomeOcean-4B with a 10240-token context. The package recently moved to the vLLM V1 engine and transformers 5.12 or later; under transformers 5, the tokenizer should be loaded with PreTrainedTokenizerFast. profile.summary: Genomics-FM is a DNA foundation model meant to cut the amount of labelled data that genomic prediction tasks need. It is a BERT-style encoder pretrained on large amounts of unlabelled DNA with an ensemble of tokenisation vocabularies (BPE and 6-mer), then fine-tuned with one task-specific vocabulary on a small labelled set. The authors apply it to genome annotation, epigenomic and expression profile prediction, and variant effect assessment.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: The model is a BERT masked language model built on the MosaicML BERT code, which uses ALiBi position biases and FlashAttention. During pretraining each sequence is tokenised either with a BPE vocabulary or as 6-mers, and a prompt token marking the vocabulary ([BPE] or [KMER]) and the position scheme ([ALIBI] or [APE]) is put in front of it. Sequences are randomly replaced by their reverse complement half the time. Training masks tokens with a probability of 0.15 for BPE input and 0.15 divided by 6 for 6-mer input, over blocks of 512 tokens, for up to 1,000,000 steps in fp16. For a downstream task the model is fine-tuned with one chosen vocabulary.

profile.summary: GenSLM (genome-scale language model) is a family of autoregressive language models that read DNA coding sequence as codons, three nucleotides per token. The foundation models were pretrained on over 110 million prokaryotic gene sequences, and a SARS-CoV-2 model was fine-tuned on 1.5 million viral genomes to track the virus's evolution and pick out variants of concern. The released code computes sequence embeddings and generates new sequences.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: GenSLMs are generative pre-trained transformers (GPT-style causal language models) with a codon-level tokeniser. The released foundation models load GPT-NeoX architecture files (the 25M file declares GPTNeoXForCausalLM with 8 layers, hidden size 512 and 8 attention heads) and a 69-token codon vocabulary, and were trained at four sizes from 25 million to 25 billion parameters with a maximum sequence length of 2,048 tokens on individual genes from BV-BRC. The 25M and 250M models were then fine-tuned on SARS-CoV-2 genomes with sequence length 10,240 tokens; the larger sizes ran out of GPU memory at that length. The paper also describes a hierarchical model in which a diffusion model guides a codon-level transformer to cover whole genomes; the README points to a separate repository for it.

steps.title: Compute embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
import numpy as np
from torch.utils.data import DataLoader
from genslm import GenSLM, SequenceDataset

model = GenSLM("genslm_25M_patric")
model.eval()
device = "cuda" if torch.cuda.is_available() else "cpu"
model.to(device)

sequences = [
    "ATGAAAGTAACCGTTGTTGGAGCAGGTGCAGTTGGTGCAAGTTGCGCAGAATATATTGCA",
    "ATTAAAGATTTCGCATCTGAAGTTGTTTTGTTAGACATTAAAGAAGGTTATGCCGAAGGT",
]
dataset = SequenceDataset(sequences, model.seq_length, model.tokenizer)
dataloader = DataLoader(dataset)

embeddings = []
with torch.no_grad():
    for batch in dataloader:
        outputs = model(
            batch["input_ids"].to(device),
            batch["attention_mask"].to(device),
            output_hidden_states=True,
        )
        emb = outputs.hidden_states[-1].detach().cpu().numpy()
        emb = np.mean(emb, axis=1)
        embeddings.append(emb)

embeddings = np.concatenate(embeddings)
print(embeddings.shape)
PY

profile.summary: MutBERT is a DNA language model for the human genome that is built to learn from genetic variation such as single nucleotide polymorphisms (SNPs). Instead of training on one reference sequence, it encodes each genome position as a probability over the four bases, taken from allele frequencies in the 1000 Genomes Project. Given a DNA sequence, it outputs per-nucleotide embeddings that can be pooled into a sequence embedding or fine-tuned for classification.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; 2.2 Probabilistic genome representation; README: 4.2 Get the embeddings

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: MutBERT is a transformer encoder trained with masked language modelling. It has 12 encoder layers and uses rotary position embeddings (RoPE) and flash attention. Each position in the input is a distribution over the bases: positions without observed variants give the reference base a probability of 1, and variable positions carry the observed allele frequencies. Because the input is a probability matrix and not a token sequence, the usual embedding look-up is replaced by a linear layer, so each position's embedding is a weighted sum of the base embeddings. During pretraining the authors apply temperature scaling to the skewed allele probabilities. The model works at single-nucleotide level with a vocabulary of A, T, C, G and five special tokens. In the README usage example, plain sequences are passed as a one-hot matrix.
sections.source_locator: Paper: 2.1 Model architecture, 2.2 Probabilistic genome representation, 2.3 Tokenization and vocabulary, 2.4; README: 4.2 Get the embeddings

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Three pretrained checkpoints share one architecture and differ only in the training data. MutBERT uses probabilistic genomes from the 1000 Genomes Project. MutBERT-Multi uses probabilistic genomes from a 100-species whole-genome alignment. MutBERT-Ref (on Hugging Face, CompBioDSA/MutBERT-Human-Ref) takes one-hot encodings of the hg38 reference and serves as the deterministic baseline. All were trained for 120 000 steps with batch size 2048 and maximum sequence length 512. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision; this page read MutBERT at a6cdc94d, MutBERT-Human-Ref at 766be54e and MutBERT-Multi at cbdab668.

sections.title: Evaluation in the paper
sections.body: The authors compared MutBERT with DNABERT-2, several Nucleotide Transformer versions and modified MutBERT variants on transcription factor binding sites (from the GUE benchmark), the Nucleotide Transformer downstream tasks and eQTL variant effect prediction. For the eQTL task they extended MutBERT's input from 512 to 2048 base pairs and trained an SVM on the embeddings. The authors report that MutBERT ranked among the top models, and that it beat the alternatives in most of the three eQTL distance categories. They note it was pretrained on 4 L20 GPUs for 6 days.

steps.title: Compute an embedding
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
import torch.nn.functional as F

from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModel

model_name = "CompBioDSA/MutBERT"
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_name)
model = AutoModel.from_pretrained(model_name, trust_remote_code=True)

dna = "ATCGGGGCCCATTA"
inputs = tokenizer(dna, return_tensors='pt')["input_ids"]

mut_inputs = F.one_hot(inputs, num_classes=len(tokenizer)).float().to("cpu")  # len(tokenizer) is vocab size
last_hidden_state = model(mut_inputs).last_hidden_state   # [1, sequence_length, 768]

# embedding with mean pooling
embedding_mean = torch.mean(last_hidden_state[0], dim=0)
print(embedding_mean.shape) # expect to be 768

# embedding with max pooling
embedding_max = torch.max(last_hidden_state[0], dim=0)[0]
print(embedding_max.shape) # expect to be 768
PY

profile.summary: OmniNA is a generative foundation model for nucleotide sequences from many species. It was pretrained on 91.7 million DNA and RNA sequences from the NCBI nucleotide database, each paired with its text annotation, so that it learns to write an annotation for a sequence. After fine-tuning, it answers questions about an input sequence in natural language, for example whether it is a promoter, or which species it comes from.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: OmniNA uses the LLaMA architecture, an auto-regressive decoder-only transformer. Sequences and annotations share one byte pair encoding tokenizer, built with SentencePiece and trained on nucleotide sequences and wiki-103 text, with 32,001 tokens. Each pretraining example is a prompt with three parts: an instruction, a nucleotide sequence and its annotation, and the model is trained to generate the text. Inputs are capped at 601 tokens. Fine-tuning casts each downstream task as a question and answer: the training file adds a question column, and the model learns to generate the answer.

sections.body: The paper and README describe three sizes. The README table gives OmniNA-66M (8 layers, 8 heads, 66 million parameters), OmniNA-330M (16 layers, 16 heads, 330 million) and OmniNA-1.7B (24 layers, 32 heads, 1.7 billion). Hugging Face holds XLS/OmniNA-66m, XLS/OmniNA-220m and XLS/OmniNA-1.7B. The XLS/OmniNA-220m configuration has 16 layers and 16 heads, the shape the README gives for OmniNA-330M, so the middle checkpoint appears to be the same model under two different size names. The model card read (1.7B) holds only a licence tag. A result should name the Hugging Face checkpoint and revision; this page read 66m at 2c5e876a, 220m at 64ea6ce7 and 1.7B at 73d208a3.

profile.summary: Borzoi is a neural network that predicts RNA-seq coverage, the read depth along genes in different cell types and tissues, directly from DNA sequence. It takes a 524 kb stretch of human or mouse genome and outputs predicted coverage for thousands of experiments in 32 bp bins. Comparing predictions for the reference and the variant sequence gives scores for a variant's effect on gene expression, splicing and polyadenylation.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; README.md: introduction

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Borzoi is a supervised model, not a language model: it is trained to reproduce measured coverage tracks. It uses the core Enformer architecture, a tower of convolution and pooling blocks followed by self-attention blocks at 128 bp resolution, then a U-net that upsamples back to 32 bp resolution. The training targets are RNA-seq coverage from ENCODE and GTEx plus the Enformer training data (CAGE, DNase-seq, ATAC-seq and ChIP-seq). Variant effects are computed from the difference between predicted coverage for the reference and the alternate sequence, summarised by statistics such as logSED for gene expression, COVR for polyadenylation and nDi for splicing.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Main, model description; README.md: introduction; legacy score_variants tutorial

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The published model is four replicates trained with identical data splits, each distributed as a human and a mouse .h5 weight file. The authors report that an ensemble of the four replicates generally performed better than any single replicate. A separate collection of smaller Mini Borzoi models, trained on subsets of data types or with architecture changes, is also published. The repository has legacy and latest data transforms; the README says the legacy transforms are similar to those used in the manuscript. A result should say which replicates were used, whether they were averaged, and which transform was applied.

profile.summary: PlantCaduceus (short name PlantCAD) is a DNA language model for flowering plants, pretrained on the genomes of 16 angiosperm species. It reads 512-bp DNA windows one nucleotide at a time, looking at both strands. Its embeddings feed small classifiers that predict translation start and stop sites and splice sites in species it was not trained on, and its masked-base likelihoods give a zero-shot score for how deleterious a single-nucleotide variant is.
profile.summary_source_locator: README: PlantCAD overview; Paper: Abstract, Introduction, Fig. 1 caption

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: PlantCaduceus uses the Caduceus architecture, which builds on the Mamba state-space sequence model and adds bi-directionality and reverse complement (RC) equivariance, so both DNA strands are modelled together. It uses single-nucleotide tokens. Pretraining is masked language modelling: 15% of positions in each 512-bp window are masked and the model is trained with cross-entropy loss on them. Following GPN, the pretraining set down-samples noncoding regions and down-weights repeats. Downstream, frozen embeddings train XGBoost or linear classifiers, and the zero-shot score is the log-likelihood difference between the reference and alternate allele at a masked position.

sections.body: PlantCAD comes in four sizes, named by their number of Caduceus blocks: PlantCaduceus_l20, l24, l28 and l32, all with a 512-bp input. The model card recommends the largest, l32, for zero-shot scoring. The same repository now also hosts PlantCAD2, a later generation with an 8192-bp input and separate checkpoints (Small, Medium, Large); it is a different model and is not covered here. A result should name the checkpoint and its Hugging Face revision; the listing read on 2026-11-26 gives l32 at e624c13c, l28 at 5ac1d5e7, l24 at 8c41e4d5 and l20 at d1b3c7d4.

sections.title: Evaluation in the paper
sections.body: The authors trained XGBoost and linear classifiers on Arabidopsis labels for translation initiation and termination sites and splice donor and acceptor sites, then tested them on species in the pretraining set (Oryza sativa, Sorghum bicolor) and outside it (Gossypium hirsutum, Glycine max, Zea mays). They compared PlantCaduceus with other DNA language models including GPN and AgroNT. For variants, they compared zero-shot scores with phyloP, phastCons, GPN and AgroNT. The claim of best cross-species performance is the authors'.

steps.title: Compute embeddings
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
import torch
from transformers import AutoTokenizer, AutoModelForMaskedLM

device = 'cuda:0'
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained('kuleshov-group/PlantCaduceus_l32')
model = AutoModelForMaskedLM.from_pretrained(
    'kuleshov-group/PlantCaduceus_l32', trust_remote_code=True
).to(device)

sequence = ""

input_ids = tokenizer.encode_plus(
    sequence, return_tensors="pt", return_attention_mask=False,
    return_token_type_ids=False
)["input_ids"].to(device)

with torch.inference_mode():
    outputs = model(input_ids=input_ids, output_hidden_states=True)

embeddings = outputs.hidden_states[-1].to(torch.float32).cpu().numpy()

# Average forward and reverse complement embeddings
hidden_size = embeddings.shape[-1] // 2
forward = embeddings[..., 0:hidden_size]
reverse = embeddings[..., hidden_size:][:, ::-1, :]
averaged_embeddings = (forward + reverse) / 2
print(averaged_embeddings.shape)
PY
steps.explanation: The README 'Quick example' wrapped in a shell heredoc. It downloads PlantCaduceus_l32, runs one 512-bp sequence on the GPU and averages the forward and reverse-complement halves of the last hidden state.

outputs: The shape of the strand-averaged embedding array: one row per token of the input sequence, with half the width of the raw hidden state. The README does not print the expected numbers.

profile.summary: SPACE is a DNA model that learns sequence representations by supervised training rather than by masked or next-token prediction. It is trained to predict thousands of genomic profiles, such as chromatin accessibility, transcription factor binding, histone marks and CAGE, from long human and mouse DNA sequences. Its encoder can then be fine-tuned or used as a feature extractor for other DNA tasks, and the full model predicts the profiles themselves.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: SPACE (Species-Profile Adaptive Collaborative Experts) keeps the Enformer setup of predicting genomic profiles from DNA, and adds two Mixture of Experts (MoE) parts. A species-aware encoder adds a trainable species embedding and routes each input sparsely across experts, so it can learn both species-specific and shared features. A profile-grouped enhancement decoder uses gated experts to model dependencies between profile types before the human and mouse output heads. The implementation is based on Enformer-Pytorch and Mod-Squad. In the released configuration the input is 131,072 bp, the model width is 1536 with 11 layers and 8 attention heads, the species MoE has 4 experts and the profile MoE has 8, and topk is set to 3.

profile.summary: AIDO.DNA, now renamed GB.DNA by its developer GenBio AI, is a large DNA language model meant as a general-purpose encoder of DNA sequence. It reads up to 4,000 nucleotides one base at a time and was pretrained on 10.6 billion nucleotides from 796 species. Its embeddings are fine-tuned or probed for tasks such as gene expression prediction, genome mining, in silico mutagenesis and sequence generation.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: AIDO.DNA is a BERT-style, encoder-only dense transformer trained with masked language modelling. It uses single-nucleotide tokens from a 5-letter vocabulary (A, T, C, G, N), with a [CLS] token at the start and an [EOS] token at the end of each sequence. The authors updated the BERT design with SwiGLU, LayerNorms and rotary positional embeddings (RoPE). The 7B model has 32 layers, 32 attention heads and hidden size 4352. Its design bet, in the authors' words, is to scale model size while keeping a short 4k context. It was trained for 100000 iterations at global batch size 1024 on 256 H100 GPUs with Megatron-LM, which took 8 days.

profile.summary: OmniReg-GPT is a generative DNA foundation model for long human genomic sequences. It reads DNA tokenised into subword units and was pretrained to predict the next token on 20 kb windows of the human T2T genome. Its embeddings are fine-tuned for regulatory tasks such as histone marks, promoters and enhancers, gene expression, chromatin accessibility and 3D chromatin contacts, and it can generate candidate enhancer sequences from a prompt.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: OmniReg-GPT is a decoder-only transformer trained with next-token prediction. DNA is tokenised with the BPE tokenizer from GENA-LM (vocabulary 32,000). The network has 12 local blocks, where each window of tokens attends to itself and the preceding window, and 2 global blocks that build a whole-sequence representation. The authors say this reduces attention cost from quadratic to linear in sequence length. It uses rotary position embeddings and FlashAttention. For downstream tasks a single vector is taken as the mean of all token embeddings.

profile.summary: SpeciesLM is a family of species-aware DNA language models for the non-coding regions that flank genes. A model reads the sequence before the start codon or after the stop codon of a gene, together with a token naming the species it came from, and predicts masked nucleotides. The published models give per-nucleotide probabilities and sequence embeddings, which the authors use to find regulatory motifs and to predict gene expression and mRNA half-life. The original models were trained on fungi; a later metazoa checkpoint is the one TraitGym scores on human variants.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; Materials and methods, Masked language modeling; README; TraitGym config/config.yaml: specieslm

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Each model is a DNABERT transformer with 12 encoder blocks. Nucleotides are split into overlapping 6-mers before entering the model. During training, spans of overlapping 6-mers are masked and the model learns to reconstruct them by minimising cross-entropy. The species label is prepended to the sequence as an extra token whose embedding is learned. An agnostic version was trained without this token for comparison. To predict for a species not seen in training, the authors give the token of a closely related species (C. glabrata for the 3' model and K. africana for the 5' model). Sequence representations come from pooling hidden states; the tutorial notebook averages hidden layers from layer 8 onwards. The later metazoa checkpoint keeps the width, depth and head count but uses a rotary-embedding variant (model_type rotarybert) with its own modelling code loaded through trust_remote_code.

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: Two sets of weights exist. The paper's fungal models are four branches of one Hugging Face repository: species and agnostic models for the 3' region (300 bp after the stop codon) and for the 5' region (1000 bp before the start codon plus the start codon). This page read downstream_species_lm at revision 742e7928 and upstream_species_lm at revision 1052abf2, taken from the branch listing. A second set is published under the johahi account: specieslm-fungi-upstream-k1, specieslm-fungi-downstream-k1, specieslm-fungi-yeastss-upstream-k1 (the sources do not describe this one) and specieslm-metazoa-upstream-k6, read here at revision 744863be. TraitGym scores that metazoa checkpoint with a 2000 bp window, so a result on this record should name the account, the checkpoint and the revision; the fungal and metazoa weights are not interchangeable. The upstream models were trained with FlashAttention and converted to standard Hugging Face models, which the README says may give slight numerical instabilities in float32.

profile.summary: Uni-RNA is a pre-trained language model for RNA sequences from DP Technology. It reads an RNA sequence and returns a learned representation (embedding) for each position, or predicted probabilities for masked positions. The authors fine-tune these representations for RNA structure and function prediction tasks.

sections.body: Uni-RNA is a Transformer encoder with a masked-language-model head: the masked-LM class outputs, for each position, logits over the token vocabulary. The last hidden layer gives per-position embeddings that can be used directly or fine-tuned for a downstream task. The training data and pre-training details are described in the preprint, whose full text was not read here.

profile.summary: Akita predicts how a stretch of DNA folds in three dimensions. It takes just over one megabase of sequence, one-hot encoded, and returns a predicted contact map for that window, as log observed over expected values, for each of five cell types it was trained on. It is used for in silico work: saturation mutagenesis, interpreting eQTLs, predicting the effect of structural variants and comparing species.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper abstract (Europe PMC record); params.json: model; targets.txt; explore_model.ipynb

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Akita is a convolutional network in two halves. A 1D trunk reads the one-hot sequence: a convolution block, then a tower of ten convolution and pooling blocks, then eight dilated residual blocks, which brings 1,048,576 bases down to 2,048 bp bins. A 2D head turns the 1D representation into a pairwise map (one_to_two with a mean operation), concatenates a distance encoding, symmetrises it, applies six dilated 2D residual blocks, crops the edges and reads off the upper triangle with a diagonal offset of 2. The final layer has five linear units, one per training dataset. Training used mean squared error with SGD, batch size 2, and reverse-complement and shift augmentation. The published model has 751,653 parameters, of which 746,149 are trainable.

The published model is a single TensorFlow checkpoint, model_best.h5, trained on human Hi-C and micro-C mapped to hg38 at 2048 bp resolution, with params.json as its configuration. It was released with TraitGym, a benchmark of causal regulatory variants in human genetics. Given a DNA window, it predicts masked nucleotides; the GPN tools turn this into a variant score, the log-likelihood ratio of the alternate against the reference allele, or into sequence embeddings.

profile.summary: CodonBERT is a language model for the coding regions of mRNA, built by Sanofi for mRNA vaccine and therapeutic design. It reads a coding sequence codon by codon and outputs an embedding for each codon. These embeddings can be fine-tuned to predict properties such as protein expression and mRNA degradation, to help choose among the many mRNA sequences that encode the same protein.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: CodonBERT is a BERT model of 12 bidirectional transformer encoder layers, each with 12 attention heads and hidden size 768. Each codon is one token: five symbols (A, U, G, C, N) in three positions give 125 codons, plus five special tokens, for a vocabulary of 130. The input is a pair of sequences joined by a separator, embedded with codon, position and segment embeddings. Pretraining combined two tasks: masked language modelling over codons, and sequence taxonomy prediction, in which the model predicts whether the two sequences come from the same one of 14 taxonomic categories. For downstream tasks, the embeddings feed additional trainable layers.

The repository holds pretraining and fine-tuning scripts, the NCBI IDs of all 10 million pretraining sequences, a held-out evaluation set, and the downstream datasets including an internal Sanofi set (MLOS.csv). profile.summary: BPNet is a convolutional neural network that predicts transcription-factor binding from DNA sequence at single-base resolution. It reads a stretch of genomic sequence and predicts the strand-specific read profile and the total read count of a ChIP-nexus or ChIP-seq experiment over that region. It is not a pretrained model: users train a new BPNet on their own experiment, then interpret it to find the sequence motifs that drive binding.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper abstract; README.md opening paragraph

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: In the paper, the body of the network is a first convolutional layer of 64 filters of width 25 bp, followed by 9 dilated convolutional layers of 64 filters of width 3, with the dilation rate doubling at every layer and no pooling, so base resolution is kept. Two output heads per transcription factor sit on top: a deconvolutional layer that predicts the probability of a read at each position on each strand (profile shape), and a global average pooling layer with a fully connected layer that predicts the total read count. The loss is a multinomial negative log-likelihood for profile shape plus a mean squared error on log total counts. A control track is given as an extra input so that experimental bias is regressed out. After training, contribution scores and TF-MoDISco are used to extract motifs.
sections.source_locator: Paper: Results, 'BPNet predicts TF binding profiles from sequence'; Methods, BPNet architecture and loss function

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: There are two generations of the code in the same repository. The original package that accompanied the paper is kept at the v0-final tag; it uses a `bpnet train` command, a dataspec.yml file and Python 3.6 with TensorFlow 1. The current master branch is described by its authors as the improved version and the one to use; it has separate `bpnet-train`, `bpnet-predict` and `bpnet-shap` commands, Python 3.7, and an example configuration with a 2114 bp input, a 1000 bp output profile, a first filter of width 21 and 8 dilated layers. The two generations use different defaults, so a result should name the code version (tag or commit), the architecture parameters file and the training data. The trained mouse ESC model from the paper (Oct4, Sox2, Nanog, Klf4) is published on Zenodo and on Kipoi as BPNet-OSKN.

profile.summary: DeCodon is a generative language model for protein-coding DNA that works one codon at a time. Given an NCBI Taxonomy ID for an organism, it writes new coding sequences for that organism. It is the decoder half of the cdsFM suite, released with the encoder model EnCodon, and was pretrained on coding sequences from the NCBI Genomes database.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: Tokens are the 64 codons, 5 special tokens and one organism token per NCBI Taxonomy ID listed in the package's taxids.txt; config.json sets vocab_size 1736. DeCodon is loaded as a causal language model: its configuration marks it as a decoder with 12 hidden layers, 16 attention heads, hidden size 1024 and rotary position embeddings. To generate, the wrapper builds a prompt from the organism's taxonomy ID in angle brackets, so the model writes a sequence conditioned on the organism, and stops at the separator token. The same wrapper also offers embedding extraction and variant scoring.

profile.summary: RFamLlama is a generative RNA language model conditioned on RNA family. Given an Rfam family ID as a prompt tag, it writes new RNA sequences of that family; the same model can also score sequences for zero-shot fitness prediction. It was trained on sequences from over 4,000 RNA families, each labelled with a family tag.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: RFamLlama is a decoder-only Llama model for causal (next-token) language modelling over a 22-token vocabulary. Each training sequence is preceded by a control tag naming its family. A prompt has the form <|bos|> <|tag_start|> family number <|tag_end|> <|5|>, where the family number is the Rfam ID without the RF prefix; the model then writes the sequence, which ends at the <|3|> token. The developers report that the family tags improve zero-shot fitness prediction; the sources read do not say how a fitness score is computed.

steps.title: Generate sequences for one Rfam family
steps.shell:
python - <<'PY'
# generation
from transformers import LlamaForCausalLM, AutoTokenizer, pipeline
import torch
import sys

model_url = "jinyuan22/RFamLlama-base"
model = LlamaForCausalLM.from_pretrained(model_url, torch_dtype=torch.float16)
tokenizer = AutoTokenizer.from_pretrained(model_url)

device = torch.device("cuda:0") if torch.cuda.is_available() else torch.device("cpu")

pipe = pipeline("text-generation", model=model, device=device, tokenizer=tokenizer)

tag = "RF00005"
txt = f"<|bos|> <|tag_start|> {tag[2:]} <|tag_end|> <|5|> "
all_outputs = []
outputs = pipe(txt, num_return_sequences=10, max_new_tokens=300, repetition_penalty=1, top_p=1,temperature=1, do_sample=True)

for i, output in enumerate(outputs):
    seq = output["generated_text"]
    seq = seq.split("<|5|>")[1].split("<|3|>")[0]
    print(f">{i}\n{seq}")
PY

profile.summary: ERNIE-RNA is a pretrained RNA language model that learns from RNA sequence alone but is given a hint about which bases could pair. It is a modified BERT model whose attention is biased by possible base pairs, trained on 20.4 million non-coding RNA sequences. Given RNA sequences up to 1024 nucleotides, it returns sequence and per-base embeddings and attention maps; the repository also ships fine-tuned heads for secondary structure, 3D closeness and 5' UTR mean ribosome load prediction.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Introduction, Fig. 1, Discussion; README: Embedding Extraction, Secondary structure prediction, 3D Closeness Prediction, UTR MRL prediction

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: ERNIE-RNA follows the BERT design: 12 transformer blocks, each with 12 attention heads over a 768-dimensional token embedding, about 86 million parameters in total. Its change is an all-against-all pairwise bias added to the attention scores, which gives the model prior knowledge of which bases could pair. It was pretrained with masked language modelling: about 15% of nucleotide tokens are replaced and the model predicts them with a cross-entropy loss. The authors report that the attention maps of the pretrained model already capture secondary structure without fine-tuning.

All are downloaded from a Google Drive folder with no version tags. A result should name the checkpoint file, the dataset_name used for structure prediction, and the repository commit; this page read commit 43bc06de.

profile.summary: UTR-LM is a language model for the 5' untranslated region (5' UTR) of mRNA, the stretch before the coding sequence that strongly affects how well an mRNA is translated. It reads a 5' UTR sequence and, after fine-tuning, predicts mean ribosome loading, translation efficiency or mRNA expression level. Pretraining combines masked language modelling with labels computed from the sequence, such as secondary structure and minimum free energy.

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: UTR-LM is built on a modified copy of the ESM-2 transformer code, shipped in the repository. The reported settings are 6 transformer layers, 16 attention heads and an embedding size of 128. Pretraining uses masked language modelling (MLM) and, in the recommended variants, also predicts the minimum free energy (MFE) and/or the secondary structure of the sequence. For downstream tasks the developers fine-tune the whole model and feed the [CLS]-token embedding to a predictor trained with Huber loss.

profile.summary: FramePool predicts how strongly a 5' untranslated region (5' UTR) drives translation, measured as mean ribosome load, directly from the 5' UTR sequence. It is a convolutional network trained on a massively parallel reporter assay, made to accept 5' UTRs of any length by pooling motif detections separately in each of the three reading frames. Through Kipoi, it takes variants from a VCF file and reports the predicted log2 fold change in mean ribosome load for each affected 5' UTR.
profile.summary_source_locator: Paper: Abstract; README; Kipoi model.yaml: info.doc

sections.title: How it works
sections.body: FramePool adapts the published MPRA model of Sample et al. That model used a dense layer, so it only worked for the sequence lengths it was trained on. FramePool keeps three convolutional layers (kernel size 7, 128 filters each, with residual skip connections) and replaces the position-specific dense input with global max and average pooling, done separately for each of the three frames relative to the start codon. The pooled values (a vector of 768) go into a dense layer of 64 neurons and a final linear output. Each model has 282,625 learnable weights; the combined model has 4 more in a scaling layer. The model was trained with the Adam optimiser and a mean squared error loss.
sections.source_locator: README; Paper: Methods, Framepool model; Model training

sections.title: Versions and reproducibility
sections.body: The paper trains three models: FramePool50 on 50-nucleotide MPRA sequences, FramePool100 on 25 to 100 nucleotide sequences, and FramePoolCombined on both, with a scaling layer for the two libraries. The paper names FramePoolCombined as the model for variant effect prediction from VCF files. The Kipoi zoo entry downloads the weights file Framepool_combined_residual.h5 from Zenodo record 3584238 with a fixed md5 checksum. A result should name the Kipoi model (Framepool), the weights checksum and the kipoi/models commit; this page read commit 770dcaf2.
